title: Gabber global projective alteration with a relative strict normal crossings boundary
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\ell$ be a prime different from $\operatorname{char}(k)$, let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $Z\subseteq X$ be a nowhere dense closed subset. There exist a finite field extension $k'/k$ of degree prime to $\ell$ [def-pc-field-extension], a smooth quasi-projective $k'$-scheme $P$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and a proper projective surjective morphism $a:P\to X$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] compatible with $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, such that $a$ sends every generic point of an irreducible component of $P$ to a generic point of an irreducible component of $X$, and induces there finite residue-field extensions of degree prime to $\ell$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-residue-field]. The reduced inverse image of $Z$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor on $P/k'$: it has finitely many distinct irreducible components $D_i$, each smooth over $k'$ and of codimension one, with every intersection $\bigcap_{i\in J}D_i$ smooth over $k'$ and of codimension $|J|$ wherever nonempty. Locally at a point of $P$, the components through that point have equations given by distinct members of a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. In particular this reduced inverse image is a strict normal crossings boundary in the regular-scheme sense [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Here quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over $k\prime$. Empty schemes, empty boundaries and empty intersections are allowed.

source.place: Expose X, Theorem 2.1 and definition of an ell-prime alteration immediately before it; printed pp. 148--149. Relative strict normal crossings is explained immediately after the theorem; VIII 4.1.2 and Remark 4.2.2(i).
